references.phrase: cofinal subset of the well-ordered ordinal α

references.context: Order theory: order isomorphism f:(A,≤_A)→(B,≤_B), a bijection preserving and reflecting order; for well-ordered sets this identifies equal ordinal order types.
references.reason: Order isomorphism of partially or well-ordered sets is independently reusable, and stronger than arbitrary bijection or order-preserving map.
references.matching_note: Preserve source's minimality of the order type in cofinality. Do not identify order isomorphism with isomorphism of groups or categories.

references.phrase: least order type and minimum-cardinality equivalence
references.disposition: These are two stated characterizations of cf(α) for a fixed ordinal, not unrelated notions or categorical functor cofinality.

references.phrase: algebraic element of E over F

references.context: Formal polynomial algebra: a nonzero element P∈F[X] of the univariate polynomial ring over field F, meaning at least one coefficient of its finite coefficient sequence is nonzero; unlike the zero polynomial it may have a well-defined nonnegative degree.
references.reason: Being a nonzero polynomial is a reusable algebraic predicate, and the existing degree-of-nonzero-polynomial meaning supplies a consequence but not the general polynomial-ring prerequisite or this nonzero condition.
references.matching_note: Compare general polynomial-algebra candidate missing.9db64b2f9cdb8258e3d8 and degree-of-nonzero-polynomial meaning.wave2.foundation.nonzero-polynomial-degree; avoid treating zero polynomial as satisfying algebraicity.

references.phrase: every element of E satisfies some polynomial
references.disposition: The defining universal quantifier is essential; this is stronger than asserting the existence of a single algebraic element.

references.phrase: R-algebra generated by finitely many elements
references.context: Commutative algebra: R-subalgebra of unital R-algebra S generated by a finite family s_1,…,s_n, the smallest unital R-subalgebra containing their elements, equal to the image of evaluation R[X_1,…,X_n]→S; its being all of S is the finite-type condition.
references.reason: Generated subalgebras are reusable constructions, distinct from the finite-type property and from finite presentation, which additionally requires finitely generated relation ideal.
references.matching_note: Compare existing finite-type ring-map meaning and polynomial-evaluation candidate missing.60dd364a1927126e153d; no self-link to finite-type meaning should be introduced.

references.context: Commutative algebra: polynomial algebra R[X_i : i in I] over a commutative unital coefficient ring R, for an arbitrary set I of independent indeterminates; each polynomial has finite monomial support. Includes the one-variable and finite-variable cases and polynomial algebras over fields and quotient coefficient rings.
references.matching_note: Reviewed original source's polynomial expression with the common multivariate-polynomial construction. Index-set size and base coefficient ring specialize the same general commutative unital polynomial algebra; do not conflate it with localization, polynomial evaluation, the polynomial quotient or degree.

references.context: Set theory: surjective function f:X→Y whose image is the entire stated codomain Y; for module homomorphisms this is the underlying-set surjectivity of the R-linear map, independent of linearity, free domain, or choice of basis.
references.matching_note: The structured ring/module map is onto its specified codomain as an underlying set map; local homomorphism, module localization or R-algebra compatibility are extra source conditions, not part of the general surjectivity prerequisite.

references.disposition: Finite type constrains the generators; finite presentation would additionally constrain relations and is not inferred.

references.phrase: finite zigzag of arrows between objects
references.context: Category theory: finite zigzag of objects x=x_0,…,x_n=y in category C with for each consecutive pair at least one morphism x_i→x_{i+1} or x_{i+1}→x_i; arrows need not be invertible, and n=0 joins x to itself.
references.reason: The finite unoriented zigzag construction is independently reusable, and is not a directed composable path or an isomorphism in the category.
references.matching_note: Connected category requires nonempty object set and a zigzag between every pair; do not identify with groupoid connectivity through isomorphisms.

references.disposition: The nonemptiness requirement is explicit; an empty category is not connected under this convention.

references.phrase: directions of zigzag arrows may alternate
references.disposition: Connectivity uses the underlying undirected incidence of morphisms, not a directed path condition.
